about: 30 sample lines and the grade the master's own lib.js grade() (line 483) gives each, recorded by grade-parity.record.mjs; grade.test.ts holds Rosie's grade() to each within 0.1, null where the master's is null (under 12 words). The lines are the master's sample cast (master-A.json: Rosie's messages, step notes, a layer line and the story), the K-03 v1 check-* and final-two-sends texts, K-01 v1 fixed lines, and four of their own (long words, a long dash and clock forms, a long sentence of commas and words with y, and Spanish).

lines.text: Hi! I'm Rosie, an automated assistant. I'll set up your business so AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini can book you. What kinds of work do you do? Just type them.
I don't have that kind of work yet, so I'll set it up from your own words and price list. First, a short checklist about your work.
Thanks for telling me. Rosie books services with a visit, so it can't set this one up. A person on our team will look at it within 1 business day.
Sam types the kinds of work in any words. Each one brings its own plug-in: its services, its questions for customers and its license rules.
Rosie drafts a plug-in from the owner's own words and price list, asking a fixed checklist. A person on Rosie's team reviews it within 1 business day.
Some work isn't a service Rosie books. That's goods with no visit, delivery only, renting a thing or space alone, or work the law bars. Rosie says so and sets nothing up.
A plug-in holds what one kind of work needs. The steps around it stay the same. Rosie loads the barbershop's now, and plumbing's and electrical's when Sam gets to them.
Only the business's clear no turns a protective fact off. Silence or a skipped block keeps it on, so its question is never hidden.
The customer's phone is away, so there's no code. Riley notes it, and DONE at the end of the visit confirms it instead.
At a class, each person booked has their own code. The desk can also tick names on the Today page, which counts as checked in.
Where the plug-in's visit is a drop-off, the code is given when the item is left. A mail-in has no code: it counts when the item arrives.
Next come the before notes, the price or the OK, and the work, as at the chair. READY and the pick-up come after.
Sam taps a link or scans a QR code on rosfield.com, and a chat with Rosie opens. Sam writes first, since that's how the chat starts.
On a call: ask for them by first name. If anyone else or a machine answers, give only the plain display name and call back later. No voicemail.

Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books Lee's Barbershop with Riley, for Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am. The service depends on the money choice you pick. Pick one at the top to follow its path from start to end.
Riley says yes.
Your visit is Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am. Does that still work? Or should we find another time?
